entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
entries.description: FDA today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis.
entries.summary: FDA approves Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection for chronic hepatitis B in adults without cirrhosis.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must update labeling, manage combination therapy, and monitor for this new biologic.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women
entries.description: Today, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first generic of Climara Pro (estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system, 0.045 mg per day/0.015 mg), a transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus applied once a week.
entries.summary: The FDA has approved the first generic version of the Climara Pro transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus, to be applied once weekly.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should update their product portfolios and labeling to reflect the availability of a generic, which may impact pricing, reimbursement, and market positioning.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today released final guidance establishing a clear framework for how drug companies can develop, distribute, and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines.
entries.summary: The FDA has issued final guidance on prescription drug apps and software, establishing a clear framework for their development, distribution, and labeling.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must review and align app development and labeling processes to meet the new FDA framework requirements.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Allow Certain Patients with Rectal Cancer to Avoid Chemotherapy, Radiation and Surgery
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for a new use of the immunotherapy Jemperli (dostarlimab-gxly) that may allow some patients with locally advanced rectal cancer to avoid common treatments that can have a lasting impact on their daily life.
entries.summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Jemperli (dostarlimab‑gxly) as a new use in locally advanced rectal cancer.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor this approval when developing labeling for rectal cancer indications and consider its impact on treatment pathways.

entries.label: MHRA
entries.title: Why post-market surveillance is a priority for the MHRA AI Airlock programme
entries.description: It is widely recognised that AI technologies have the potential to positively transform healthcare by improving patient outcomes, supporting clinical decision-making and helping health services work more efficiently. However, AI systems can behave differently once they move from controlled testing …
entries.summary: The MHRA AI Airlock programme highlights post‑market surveillance as a priority.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must recognize that AI systems may behave differently after deployment and therefore need to incorporate ongoing monitoring into their post‑market surveillance plans.

entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a division within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to reimagine the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases.

entries.title: Qualifying notice for Hernexeos (304237)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada issued a Notice of Compliance with Conditions for Hernexeos (304237), requiring the sponsor to conduct additional studies to confirm clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must track the NOC/c and ensure the sponsor completes the mandated studies to maintain market authorization.

entries.label: WHO
entries.title: New WHO technical package to help countries improve health data for COVID-19 response and beyond
entries.description:
Today, as part of its commitment to strengthening health information systems and improving health[1], especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, WHO announced a new approach to improving access to life-saving data: the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package. The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the urgent need for timely and reliable data to drive strategic health action. Too many countries still lack both the infrastructure to routinely gather health data and the analytical capacity to use these data for effective health actions and emergency response.

“Countries must be able to measure progress to make progress,” said WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. “Particularly during COVID-19, reliable data is the best way to coordinate response efforts and improve health in all areas.”

Accurate health data are necessary to understand specific country needs in order to improve health and save lives. Data also helps direct scarce resources to where they are needed most.

The SCORE (Survey, Count, Optimize, Review, Enable) Technical Package aims to improve the availability of timely, reliable, validated, and comparable health data. For the first time in a single, harmonized package, it represents all the key elements for optimized health information system performance. Simply put, SCORE will help governments around the globe set benchmarks and i
entries.summary: WHO has released the SCORE for Health Data Technical Package to improve access to timely, reliable health data.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware of this new guideline to ensure health data collection and analysis supports regulatory submissions and emergency response.

entries.label: FDA

entries.description: The FDA today issued a direct final rule that updates its regulations to clarify that non-animal methods can be used where appropriate for testing the safety of drugs and biological products intended for human use before they’re tried in humans.
